project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration and Protection in the Clarke-Connors Range, Fitzroy Region, Central Queensland
project_summary: This project will work with landholders to protect and improve the quality and connectivity of koala habitat across 2000 hectares in the Clarke-Connors Range, Central Queensland. The project will deliver weed control to reduce fire risk and promote the growth of native species, fencing and grazing management to allow natural regeneration of trees, and fire planning and actions to reduce fire risk to both koala, and areas of koala habitat. The project will engage First Nations to understand priorities and capacity to lead and participate in the design and delivery of koala conservation actions including koala monitoring and habitat restoration actions.

project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration in Sarina, Central Queensland coastal area
project_summary: This project will improve the quality, extent and connectivity of koala habitat in the Sarina region (located within the Mackay Regional Council area) by: engaging with local landowners to increase connectivity of koala habitat through revegetation projects to establish 27 hectares of habitat; improving habitat through 150 hectares of weed management; and motivating landholders to become involved in koala conservation activities through landholder events and targeted communications and engagement. Work to extend, expand and improve nature corridors will continue to enable Sarina koalas to travel between coastal habitat and inland ranges.

project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration and Protection in Gympie, Burnett Mary.
project_summary: This project will deliver on-ground actions to protect and restore priority koala habitat. This will support the recovery of the Gympie koala population. Over 178 hectares of new koala habitat will be established through revegetation projects on private land. Natural regeneration of koala habitat will be supported by 155 hectares of weed control, with a further 23 hectares of strategic fencing installed to reduce threats of koala habitat from stock. A monitoring regime will measure the impact of these activities on koala populations and on habitat condition. Community groups, researchers and traditional owners will work with landholders to share knowledge, with a collective aim of restoring critical habitat and connectivity of the Gympie koala population.

project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration and Protection in Grandchester and Flinders Peak, SEQLD.
project_summary: This project will improve habitat quality, extent and connectivity for koalas within the Grandchester and Flinders Peak areas of South East Queensland. The project will partner with land managers and local communities to address koala habitat loss, fragmentation and degradation. On ground actions include 70 hectares of revegetation, 240 hectares of weed control, 20 hectares management of grazing pressures, and activities to support fire management to protect critical koala habitat from fire. These actions will be supported by community and landholder engagement activities, including events, workshops and direct activities on their properties. Project success will be measured through a monitoring program for koala populations and koala habitat improvements.

project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration and Protection in the Northern Tablelands, NSW.
project_summary: This project will deliver on-ground actions to improve the quality, quantity, and connectivity of koala habitat in the Armidale region of the Northern Tablelands. Revegetation projects with local landholders, land managers and the community will create 50 hectares of new koala habitat. The quality of habitat across a further 70 hectares will be improved through supported natural regeneration and improved grazing management practices. Targeted weed control of lantana, blackberry, and hawthorn across 340 hectares will restore koala habitat, and enable increased movement of koalas across the landscape. The project will build community members skills, knowledge, and capacity to deliver best practice on-ground koala conservation actions.

project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration and Protection in the Coffs Harbour - North Bellingen Area of Regional Koala Significance (ARKS), NSW
project_summary: This project engages landholders, local and NSW governments to protect and restore priority koala habitat in the Coffs Harbour and Bellingen Local Government Areas. The project will create 80 hectares of new koala habitat and improve the quality of a further 350 hectares of existing habitat through weed management and mitigation of livestock impacts. Another 30 hectares will be protected through fire management, including cultural burning. These actions will be supported by land management agreements, with detailed site management plans. Community participation will be encouraged with landholders invited to report koala sightings, get involved in koala workshops, and through involvement in koala restoration activities on their properties.

project_title: Koala Habitat Restoration and Protection in the Southern Highlands and Southern Tablelands Area of Regional Koala Significance (ARKS), NSW
project_summary: This project will deliver on-ground actions to improve the quality, quantity, and connectivity of koala habitat in the Southern Tablelands and Southern Highlands of New South Wales. The project will create 58.5 hectares of new koala habitat. A further 121 hectares of koala habitat will be improved through weed control. Fencing of over 29 kilometres will be established and 1050 hectares of feral herbivore control undertaken to reduce browsing pressure on koala habitat. Community awareness and education will be supported through 5 community engagement events. A partnership with First Nations people and the Local Land Council will be supported by training to share knowledge on koala conservation.

delivery_partner: World Wide Fund for Nature - Australia
project_title: Koalas Forever Northern Rivers Recovery Hub Restoration
project_summary: The project will deliver koala habitat restoration and create new koala habitat in cleared and burnt priority koala meta-populations within the Northern Rivers, NSW. Local landholders will be supported to expand and restore more than 630 hectares of koala habitat through revegetation of 135,000 koala trees, targeted weed control, stock removal through fencing, and drone seeding of landslip areas. The project has a strong community focus supported by 12 community workshops, planting days and citizen science monitoring programs. The project also works with First Nations peoples who will share their knowledge to undertake cultural burning across 30 hectares in the North-east Hinterland, to assist landholders to better protect koalas on their properties.

delivery_partner: NSW Department of Planning and Environment (DPE)
project_title: Bring back the bush for koalas on the Mid North Coast.
project_summary: This project will create, restore and connect isolated and degraded areas of Koala habitat in the Forster, Comboyne and South Taree areas of the Mid-North Coast. Restoration activities aim to improve connectivity to encourage greater and safer movement of koalas in this area. This will be supported through restoration of 300 hectares of koala habitat, revegetation of 150 hectares and 50 hectares of cultural burning to improve habitat condition. The delivery of 3 community events will motivate landholders to become involved in koala conservation activities, with at least 40 landholders to be engaged in koala habitat restoration on their properties.

project_title: RSPCA Queensland Wildlife Centre of Excellence
project_summary: This project will support the delivery of a Wildlife Centre for Excellence. This wildlife hospital will feature teaching facilities, information and education facilities and improved onsite rehabilitation facilities, particularly for koalas. The project will also involve planting browse and rehabilitation plantations onsite for the improved care and rehabilitation of koalas. The facility will allow the RSPCA to develop research and education partnerships that will benefit the koala.

project_title: Together for Koalas: Our Action, Their Future
project_summary: This project will increase the capability of current rescue and veterinary resources to support immediate koala health needs, as well as support operational efficiency and sustainability ahead of the opening of the new Wildlife Hospital and Centre of Excellence facility.

delivery_partner: Port Stephens Koala & Wildlife Preservation Society Limited
project_title: Port Stephens Koala Hospital (PSKH) Upgrade and Operational Expansion
project_summary: This project will support the delivery partner to expand its koala hospital and services. This will include employing vet staff, upgrading hospital infrastructure for treating koalas, expanding training for vet personnel and citizens in koala and wildlife care, establishing a eucalypt plantation and conducting research into koala disease.

project_title: Koala Preservation through Treatment, Rehabilitation & Applied Research
project_summary: This project will support the delivery partner to expand its wildlife hospital and services. This will include establishing a koala Intensive Care Unit and koala rehabilitation and exercise enclosures, extending eucalypt plantations, purchasing a new ambulance and conducting applied koala research.

project_title: Australia Zoo Wildlife Hospital Upgrade Project
project_summary: This project will support the delivery partner to expand its wildlife hospital and services. This will include employing more vet staff, conducting training and research into koala disease and purchasing land to construct a larger infectious disease ward for koalas and accommodation for staff. It will also include expanding eucalypt plantations and upgrading the hospital’s computer network and public education facilities.

project_title: Developing a koala chlamydial vaccine through to product registration
project_summary: This project will support the delivery partner to conduct further research and testing of their koala chlamydia vaccine, to progress it towards APVMA registration.

project_title: Development of vaccine implants to protect koalas against chlamydia
project_summary: This project will develop and trial an implant to deliver a chlamydia vaccine to koalas. The project will test a vaccine implant technology which is given at the time of primary vaccination. A booster vaccination is then automatically delivered 4-5 weeks later without the need for recapture.
